purpose.summary: This program defines a large table of function-key labels in three languages (French, German, English) for up to 100 function-key slots. It appears to be a data-definition module (or shared working-storage segment) that supplies multilingual key-label strings to a larger interactive application. The PROCEDURE DIVISION is minimal (only 1 PERFORM), suggesting the real work is done by callers referencing these data structures.

IBM PC box-drawing characters in comments (code page 437/850), decoded as latin-1
Inline annotation markers (<--, !) on data items indicating special/disabled entries
308 PIC clauses, all PIC X(7) — purely alphanumeric data definitions

verdict.notes: File was decoded with latin-1; box-drawing characters in comments are consistent with IBM PC code page 437/850 used in DOS-era Micro Focus or similar PC COBOL environments. The source is truncated at 16000 chars so the PROCEDURE DIVISION content is not visible, but the single PERFORM count and the nature of the file strongly suggest this is a data-definition/initialization module for a larger multilingual interactive (screen-based) application, likely HR/payroll. The '!' and '<--' annotations on some data items appear to be developer notes marking disabled or special-purpose keys.
